title: What Happens When You Get Goosebumps?
sources: Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials, 'Why You Have Goosebumps on Your Skin' (Feb 24, 2025; expert: Sara Fandino, APRN) (goosebumps, or piloerections, are an involuntary, automatic reaction that occurs whenever your sympathetic nervous system (or fight-or-flight mode) is triggered; tiny muscles contract at the base of each hair follicle, hairs stand up and small bumps form; triggers: cold, intense or sudden fear, shock, anger or excitement, music/movies ('psychogenic shivers', frisson); in animals the hair stands on end so they look larger to predators, e.g. a cat that puffs up while it hisses; in humans they don't appear to have much purpose beyond helping conserve heat; goosebumps themselves are nothing to worry about): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/why-do-you-get-goosebumps

NIH Research Matters, 'What goosebumps are for' (July 2020, on Shwartz et al., Cell 2020, Ya-Chieh Hsu lab, Harvard) (goosebumps might play two roles: making hair rise in the short term and triggering more hair growth by stem cells in the long term; the sympathetic nerve connects directly to hair follicle stem cells, with the arrector pili muscle as a bridge; mice exposed to cold started to produce new hairs from their stem cells in less than two weeks; findings are in mice): https://www.nih.gov/news-events/nih-research-matters/what-goosebumps-are

Tease (next video): NINDS 'Paresthesia Information Page' (temporary paresthesia, a feeling of 'pins and needles', when you sit with legs crossed too long or fall asleep on an arm; caused by sustained pressure on a nerve; goes away once the pressure is relieved): https://www.brainfacts.org/Diseases-and-Disorders/Neurological-Disorders-AZ/Diseases-A-to-Z-from-NINDS/Paresthesia

lines.text: What happens when you get goosebumps?
They might have two jobs, and job two is wild.
lines.caps: THEY *MIGHT HAVE | *2 JOBS | AND JOB *2 | IS *WILD

lines.text: A chill or scare flips your fight-or-flight switch,
and a tiny muscle at the base of each hair squeezes.
lines.caps: AND A *TINY | *MUSCLE AT THE | *BASE OF EACH | HAIR *SQUEEZES

lines.text: Your hairs stand on end, and bumps pop up.
lines.caps: YOUR HAIRS *STAND | ON *END, AND | *BUMPS POP UP

lines.text: That's how a hissing cat puffs up to look bigger.
lines.caps: *THAT'S HOW A | HISSING *CAT | *PUFFS UP TO | LOOK *BIGGER

lines.text: On you, it mostly just helps trap a little heat.
lines.caps: ON *YOU, IT | *MOSTLY JUST | HELPS *TRAP | A LITTLE *HEAT

lines.text: Job two? In mice left in the cold,
those goosebump nerves woke up hair stem cells,
and new hair grew in under two weeks.
